87	    local worker_pid=$!
88	    echo "$worker_pid" > "${pool_dir}/${pid_subdir}/${slot_id}.pid"
89	    _ORCH_LOCAL_LAST_SLOT_ID="$slot_id"
90	    echo "$slot_id"
91	    return 0
92	}
93	
94	# _orch_local_collect_results <pool_dir> <pid_subdir> <timeout_s>
95	# Polls .exit files for every slot in <pool_dir>/<pid_subdir>/; streams
96	# stdout/stderr. Returns the normalised orch contract code:
97	#   0 = all dispatched work units exited 0  (pool dir removed)
98	#   1 = otherwise (pool dir preserved); _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME says which —
99	#       `failed` (all exited non-zero) or `partial` (at least one passed).
100	#       #1850 (ADR-054 §4): `partial` used to be rc 2.

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# scripts/lib/proc-group.sh — process-group resolution and kill helpers.
3	# Extracted from core/router/route.sh (Wave 15-G, #687) so the test stage and
4	# any other long-running spawn share one implementation (#1748).
5	# Sourced library: no set -euo pipefail.
6	
7	[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_PROC_GROUP_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
8	_ZBUILD_PROC_GROUP_LOADED=1
9	
10	# #2056: there is no setsid prefix any more. Process groups come from `set -m`
11	# at the spawn site — bash job control makes a backgrounded job a group leader,
12	# which is POSIX and identical on macOS and Linux.
13	#
14	# `setsid -w` was wrong here twice over. It is absent on macOS (util-linux is
15	# keg-only), so the prefix went empty, no group was created, and an abort
16	# degraded to a single-PID kill while every descendant survived — the Wave 15-G
17	# guarantee held on Linux only, and the test covering it is Linux-only too, so
18	# nothing said so. And `-w` forces setsid to fork, because it waits for the
19	# child and returns its exit status, so the pid the caller captured was the
20	# wrapper rather than the new session leader.
21	#
22	# Do not reintroduce a prefix here. A spawn that needs an external binary to get
23	# a process group is a spawn whose guarantee is platform-conditional.
24	
25	# Prints the PGID safe to signal for <pid>, or nothing. Empty is not "no group":
26	# it means the group could not be proven distinct from ours, and signalling it
27	# would take down the runner itself — so callers must fall back to a PID kill.
28	zbuild_pg_resolve() {
29	    local _pid="${1:-}"
30	    [[ -n "$_pid" && "$_pid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
31	    local _child _self
32	    _child="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$_pid" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
33	    _self="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$$" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
34	    if [[ -n "$_child" && -n "$_self" && "$_child" != "$_self" ]]; then
35	        printf '%s' "$_child"
36	        return 0
37	    fi
38	    # A short-lived child can exit before `ps` reports it. Under `set -m` the
39	    # spawn IS the group leader, so PGID == PID by construction and that stays
40	    # true after it is gone — reporting the pid is correct, not a guess.
41	    #
42	    # This branch previously justified itself with "setsid execs in place, so it
43	    # needs no fork". That was false under `-w` (#2056): setsid forks in order to
44	    # wait, so the captured pid was the wrapper and the group belonged to a
45	    # process one fork below. Under job control there is no wrapper to be wrong
46	    # about.
47	    if [[ -z "$_child" ]]; then
48	        printf '%s' "$_pid"
49	    fi
50	}
51	
52	# TERM <target>, then KILL whatever is left after <grace_s>. Shared by the group
53	# and single-PID paths so both get the same grace — the escalation is the whole
54	# contract, and a caller that skips it is indistinguishable from a plain KILL.
55	#
56	# Synchronous by construction (#905): the `{ sleep 1 && kill -KILL; } &` backstop
57	# this replaces could outlive the caller that armed it, so teardown returned
58	# while the tree was still alive and the backstop was sometimes lost with it.
59	# Polling instead costs milliseconds when the target exits on TERM, costs the
60	# full grace only when it ignores TERM, and leaves nothing running on return.
61	_zbuild_pg_term_then_kill() {
62	    # `--` because a group target is spelled `-PGID` and would otherwise parse
63	    # as an option.
64	    local _target="$1" _grace="$2"
65	    kill -TERM -- "$_target" 2>/dev/null || true
66	    local _ticks=$(( _grace * 10 )) _i=0
67	    while (( _i < _ticks )); do
68	        kill -0 -- "$_target" 2>/dev/null || return 0
69	        sleep 0.1 2>/dev/null || true
70	        _i=$(( _i + 1 ))
71	    done
72	    kill -KILL -- "$_target" 2>/dev/null || true
73	}
74	
75	# A non-numeric grace would evaluate to 0 in the arithmetic context above, so the
76	# poll loop would never run and the target would go straight to KILL — silently
77	# losing the escalation the caller asked for. Clamp to the default instead.
78	_zbuild_pg_grace() {
79	    local _g="${1:-1}"
80	    [[ "$_g" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$_g" -gt 0 ]] && printf '%s' "$_g" || printf '1'
81	}
82	
83	# zbuild_pg_record_pgid <file> — the pgid out of a `.pgid` record.
84	#
85	# ONE reader, because there are two formats on disk and three places that read
86	# them (#2018). The engine's dispatch record is `<pgid>\t<leader start time>`;
87	# tool/test's own `test-stage.pgid` is a bare number; and a record written before
88	# #2018 is bare too. A reader that only understands one of those does not error —
89	# it fails the numeric guard and `continue`s, so the caller kills NOTHING and
90	# reports success. That is how a format change here silently disables ADR-062 §2
91	# reclamation, which is the path that actually runs on every normal exit.
92	#
93	# Prints nothing and returns 1 when there is no usable pgid, so a caller can
94	# still distinguish "no record" from "record says 1234".
95	zbuild_pg_record_pgid() {
96	    local _f="${1:-}" _pgid=""
97	    [[ -n "$_f" && -f "$_f" ]] || return 1
98	    IFS=$'\t' read -r _pgid _ 2>/dev/null < "$_f" || true
99	    [[ "$_pgid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 1
100	    printf '%s' "$_pgid"
101	}
102	
103	# zbuild_pg_register <pgid> — record a process group the caller just created.
104	#
105	# ADR-062 §1 had the ENGINE record this at dispatch. It could not, and the reason
106	# is structural: a stage is a bash function call, not a subprocess, so at the
107	# dispatch seam no group exists yet. That code fell back to `$$`'s group — the
108	# engine's own — which teardown then skipped, correctly, because signalling your
109	# own group takes the runner down with it. Every record was unkillable, every
110	# record was skipped, and §2's kill loop never freed anything (#2024).
111	#
112	# So the direction reverses: whoever CREATES a group registers it. Two sites do,
113	# and only two — `tool/test`'s `set -m` suite and the router's `setsid` spawn.
114	#
115	# Refusing to register our own group is the invariant, not a safety check. A
116	# record naming the registrar's own group is strictly worse than no record: it
117	# cannot be acted on, and it makes the mechanism look live while it does nothing
118	# — which is exactly how the original defect survived #2001, #2018 and an ADR.
119	#
120	# Fail-open throughout: a spawn is never refused because bookkeeping was
121	# unavailable. Silence here costs a possible leak; failing here costs the run.
122	zbuild_pg_register() {
123	    local _pgid="${1:-}"
124	    [[ -n "$_pgid" && "$_pgid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
125	    local _self
126	    _self="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$$" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
127	    [[ -n "$_self" && "$_self" == "$_pgid" ]] && return 0
128	    local _sd="${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR:-}"
129	    [[ -n "$_sd" && -d "$_sd" ]] || return 0
130	    local _stage="${2:-${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}}"
131	    [[ -n "$_stage" ]] || return 0
132	    # One path component, sanitised the same way stage scratch keys are, so no
133	    # stage name can climb out of runtime/.
134	    _stage="${_stage//[^A-Za-z0-9_-]/_}"
135	    local _dir="${_sd}/runtime/stages"
136	    mkdir -p "$_dir" 2>/dev/null || return 0
137	    # #2018 format: the leader's start time proves the pgid still names what
138	    # recorded it, so a later sweep cannot signal a recycled pid.
139	    local _start
140	    _start="$(ps -o lstart= -p "$_pgid" 2>/dev/null | tr -s ' ' | sed 's/^ *//;s/ *$//' || true)"
141	    printf '%s\t%s' "$_pgid" "$_start" > "${_dir}/${_stage}.pgid" 2>/dev/null || true
142	    return 0
143	}
144	
145	# TERM then KILL a whole process group. `-PGID` is the negative-pid convention.
146	zbuild_pg_kill() {
147	    local _pgid="${1:-}"
148	    [[ -n "$_pgid" && "$_pgid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
149	    # Refuse our own group: `kill -- -PGID` from inside it takes down the runner.
150	    local _self
151	    _self="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$$" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
152	    [[ -n "$_self" && "$_self" == "$_pgid" ]] && return 0
153	    _zbuild_pg_term_then_kill "-$_pgid" "$(_zbuild_pg_grace "${2:-}")"
154	}
155	
156	# TERM then KILL a single PID — the path taken when no group could be proven.
157	# It gets the same grace as the group path: a suite that flushes coverage or
158	# writes partial results on SIGTERM needs the window wherever it is killed from.
159	zbuild_pid_kill() {
160	    local _pid="${1:-}"
161	    [[ -n "$_pid" && "$_pid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
162	    _zbuild_pg_term_then_kill "$_pid" "$(_zbuild_pg_grace "${2:-}")"
163	}

1	# ADR-011: Pluggable Backends (Memory, Orchestrator, Cache)
2	
3	**Status:** Accepted
4	**Amended:** 2026-08-22 — retention: the cache store is reclaimable, the memory store never is
5	**Date:** 2026-05-24
6	
7	> **Memory split:** The "memory backend" in this ADR is **learning memory** —
8	> patterns extracted from past runs, vector embeddings of source code,
9	> architectural decisions, skill-success scores. It accumulates over time and
10	> spans pipelines.
11	>
12	> It is **NOT** pipeline-resume memory (which is defined by
13	> [ADR-006](ADR-006-resume-contract.md) and transported by
14	> [ADR-010](ADR-010-ci-cli-parity.md) cache backends). Resume state is
15	> operational ("continue at stage X iteration Y"); learning memory is
16	> educational ("similar issues in the past took 3 cycles to converge").
17	>
18	> The two memory models share no storage and have independent failure modes:
19	> learning memory can be totally unavailable and pipelines still resume
20	> correctly; resume memory can be wiped and pipelines still benefit from
21	> learned patterns on the next fresh run.
22	
23	## Context
24	
25	Three cross-cutting capabilities can be implemented multiple ways, and zBuild should not pick one implementation in core:
26	
27	1. **Memory backend** — where learned patterns, embeddings, and decisions live. Could be local SQLite, ruflo's HNSW vector store via MCP, a future cloud KV, etc.
28	2. **Orchestrator backend** — how parallel agents are spawned and coordinated. Could be plain bash subshells, ruflo's hive-mind, a future job-queue worker pool, etc.
29	3. **Cache backend** — where durable state persists across CI runs (covered in ADR-010); same pattern.
30	
31	User requirement: "I want the option to use ruflo memory and ruflo swarming/hive abilities — those are not hard dependencies early on but they need to be able to do it in the future, so the architecture needs to be set to handle that."
32	
33	Translation: ship working defaults that need zero external services; let ruflo (or anything else) drop in via the plugin contract.
34	
35	## Decision
36	
37	Each capability gets a **backend contract** (a fixed set of function names + I/O shapes). A "backend" is just a plugin (`kind: tool`, with `provides.role: memory-backend` etc.) that implements the contract. zBuild ships defaults; users select alternates via `.zbuild/config.yaml`.
38	
39	### Memory backend contract
40	
41	```bash
42	memory_put <namespace> <key> <value>                 # store
43	memory_get <namespace> <key>                          # → value or empty
44	memory_search <namespace> <query> [--limit N]         # → list of matches
45	memory_list_namespaces                                # → list of strings
46	memory_namespace_exists <namespace>                   # exit 0/1
47	memory_namespace_clear <namespace>                    # destructive cleanup
48	```
49	
50	Optional (backends MAY implement; callers MUST handle absence):
51	```bash
52	memory_search_vector <namespace> <embedding>          # vector similarity search
53	memory_capabilities                                   # → JSON of declared capabilities
54	```
55	
56	**Default implementation**: `plugins/tool/memory-sqlite/` — local SQLite at `~/.zbuild/state/memory.db`, TF-IDF text search via `LIKE %query%`, no vector support. Always works, no external deps.
57	
58	**Optional implementation**: `plugins/tool/memory-ruflo/` — proxies to ruflo MCP for HNSW vector search. Requires `ruflo` binary on PATH; `memory_capabilities` declares `["vector_search", "hnsw"]`.
59	
60	### Orchestrator backend contract
61	
62	```bash
63	orch_spawn <pool_id> <count> <role_arg>               # spawn N workers
64	orch_dispatch <pool_id> <task_json>                   # send work to pool
65	orch_collect <pool_id> [--timeout S]                  # gather results; exit 0=all pass, 1=all fail, 2=partial
66	orch_shutdown <pool_id>                               # cleanup
67	orch_capabilities                                     # → JSON
68	```
69	
70	**(superseded 2026-10-08 by ADR-054 §4 / #1850 — now `orch_collect` returns 0 (all passed) or 1, naming mixed results on `_ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME=partial`)**
71	
72	**`orch_collect` exit code convention (all implementations must honour this):**
73	- `0` — all dispatched work units exited 0 (success); pool dir removed.
74	- `1` — all dispatched work units exited non-zero (complete failure).
75	- `2` — mixed results: at least one unit passed and at least one failed (partial). **(superseded 2026-10-08 by ADR-054 §4 / #1850 — now rc 1 + `_ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME=partial`)**
76	
77	Work-unit exit codes are normalised — individual codes are not passed through. Strategies use `2` to emit `stage.fail reason=partial` via the runner. **(superseded 2026-10-08 by ADR-054 §4 / #1850 — now rc 1 + `_ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME=partial`)**
78	
79	**Phase 0.5 default implementation**: `plugins/tool/orch-sequential/` — single-process, in-order dispatch. Chosen as the default for Phase 0.5 because it has zero coordination surface and the smallest reference impl of the 0/1/2 normalisation contract. The `.zbuild/config.yaml` snippet below shows how to opt in to one of the optional backends.
80	
81	**Parallel implementation**: `plugins/tool/orch-bash-parallel/` — uses bash subshells + `wait -n` for parallelism, no coordination beyond independent execution. Implements `fanout` and `sequential` strategies trivially; `composite` works via a single subshell.
82	
83	**Optional implementation**: `plugins/tool/orch-ruflo-hive/` — proxies to `ruflo hive-mind init/spawn/orchestrate`. Implements all three strategies natively; provides queen-collapse synthesis and shared-memory namespacing. `orch_capabilities` declares `["hive_mind", "queen_collapse", "shared_memory"]`.
84	
85	### Cache backend contract (covered in ADR-010)
86	
87	```bash
88	cache_pull <key> <dest_dir>                           # restore from cache key into dest_dir
89	cache_push <key> <src_dir>                            # snapshot src_dir under cache key
90	cache_capabilities                                    # → JSON
91	```
92	
93	The `<key>` is an opaque, plugin-agnostic identifier (e.g., a slot id or a content hash). The `<dest_dir>` / `<src_dir>` makes the caller's intent explicit and lets a single cache backend serve multiple consumers (resume snapshot, build artifact, etc.) within one run.
94	
95	Reconciled with the code (`core/cache/contract.sh`) on 2026-05-26 per #310: the initial sketch used a single-arg `cache_pull <slot_id>` that conflated key and destination. The two-arg form is what every implementation already needs and what the existing `gh-actions-cache` / `cache-local` plugins ship.
96	
97	Defaults: `local` — a real filesystem-backed cache under `$ZBUILD_CACHE_DIR` (defaults to `~/.zbuild/cache`). Optionals: `gh-actions-cache`, `s3`, `gist`.
98	
99	### Backend selection: `.zbuild/config.yaml`
100	
101	> **Scope note:** backend pluggability covers **memory, orchestrator, and cache only**. Model routing is core per ADR-003 — `core/router/route.sh` is not a backend and is not selectable via this config.
102	
103	```yaml
104	backends:
105	  memory: sqlite                    # default; or "ruflo"
106	  orchestrator: sequential          # default; or "bash-parallel", "ruflo-hive"
107	  cache: local                      # default; or "gh-actions-cache", "s3"
108	
109	# Optional per-backend config
110	memory_ruflo:
111	  mcp_server: "ruflo"
112	  namespace_prefix: "zbuild"
113	  fallback_to_default_on_error: true
114	
115	orchestrator_ruflo:
116	  topology: hierarchical
117	  max_agents: 8
118	  hive_timeout_sec: 300
119	```
120	
121	Resolution at startup: read config, look up the named backend in the plugin registry, verify it implements the contract. If a backend is selected but missing, `zbuild doctor` flags it. **Critical**: when a non-default backend is selected, callers MUST handle `_capabilities` differences (e.g., don't request `memory_search_vector` from the SQLite default).
122	
123	### Graceful degradation rules
124	
125	1. **Default backend always works.** Out-of-box experience requires nothing more than `./install.sh` (per ADR-023).
126	2. **Optional backend can be configured but unavailable at runtime** (e.g., ruflo daemon crashed). Each backend declares `fallback_to_default_on_error: true|false`. If true, runtime falls back to default with a `backend.degraded` event; if false, hard-fails with a clear error.
127	3. **Backend capabilities are declarative.** Callers query `<backend>_capabilities` and choose a code path based on what's available. Example: pipeline-intelligence might do vector search if `vector_search` is in capabilities, TF-IDF otherwise.
128	
129	### Plugin manifest extension
130	
131	Memory and orchestrator backends are `kind: tool` plugins with a special `provides.role`:
132	
133	```yaml
134	# plugins/tool/memory-sqlite/manifest.yaml
135	id: memory-sqlite
136	kind: tool
137	provides:
138	  role: memory-backend                  # marks as backend implementation
139	  capabilities: [text_search, namespacing, persistence]
140	
141	# plugins/tool/memory-ruflo/manifest.yaml
142	id: memory-ruflo
143	kind: tool
144	provides:
145	  role: memory-backend
146	  capabilities: [text_search, vector_search, hnsw, namespacing, persistence, distributed]
147	requires:
148	  bin: [ruflo]                          # NEW manifest field: required binaries
149	```
150

1	# ADR-017: Per-Stage Router Configuration
2	
3	**Status:** Accepted (2026-05-29)
4	**Date:** 2026-05-29
5	**Amended:** 2026-08-09 (#1820, ADR-054) — noting that #1816 inserts the manifest layer into ADR-017's resolution chain; per-stage router config is now resolved through the manifest-declared data path before falling through to the template/global config tiers documented here.
6	
7	## Context
8	
9	The router (`core/router/route.sh::route_to_model`) treats every LLM call
10	identically: same timeout, same tier resolution path, same budget posture,
11	regardless of which pipeline stage invoked it. The single global default
12	at `core/router/route.sh:48`:
13	
14	```bash
15	local secs="${ZBUILD_ROUTER_TIMEOUT:-300}"
16	```
17	
18	is the only knob, and the only escape hatch is the session-wide
19	`ZBUILD_ROUTER_TIMEOUT` env var.
20	
21	That uniformity was fine when every stage's prompt was roughly the same
22	shape. It is no longer fine. Stages have very different workloads:
23	
24	- **plan** sends a small prompt (intake goal + scope context), gets a
25	  structured JSON response, typically completes in 100–180s on Sonnet.
26	  300s is comfortable headroom.
27	- **build** sends the full plan + scope manifest + redaction context and
28	  expects a multi-file diff response. Empirically the prompt is the
29	  largest in the pipeline, the response is the largest, and 300s catches
30	  the easy cases but not the median.
31	- **review** sends a verdict prompt with the plan + diff and expects a
32	  small `{verdict, confidence, ...}` payload. Faster than plan.
33	
34	Dogfood evidence from run `20260529124603-91950` on the live install:
35	`router.error rc=124 reason=claude_cli_failed` at exactly 300s after the
36	build-stage route. Retry returned an empty response (`input_tokens=0
37	output_tokens=0`). Build plugin wrote an empty diff. Review correctly
38	blocked. The chain was faithful, but the operator burned 5+ minutes of
39	wall-time before learning that the build prompt needed more headroom.
40	
41	The naïve fix is to raise the global default. That's blunt:
42	
43	- 300 → 600 doubles the failure-detection latency on plan and review
44	  stages where the original 300s was already generous.
45	- It doesn't actually express the operator's intent. The intent is
46	  *"build needs more time than plan does"*, not *"every stage gets more
47	  time."*
48	
49	The architectural pattern for this kind of per-stage knob is already
50	established by ADR-015 v3, which added `io.destinations`, `io.tail_lines`,
51	and `io.redact` to the per-stage template block. Each is plumbed through:
52	
53	1. Awk parser arm in `_tpl_parse_stage_data` (template.sh:107-145).
54	2. Name-mangled env var `_TPL_STAGE_<KNOB>_${safe_id}`, exported for
55	   plugin subshell inheritance (#448 lesson).
56	3. Accessor function `template_stage_<knob>` (template.sh:152-160).
57	4. Validator (`_tpl_validate_io_knobs`, template.sh:119-150).
58	5. Consumer reads the accessor with a fall-back chain.
59	
60	Adding a per-stage **router** configuration surface in the template is
61	the same pattern applied to a new sibling block. The router becomes
62	stage-aware via the already-exported `ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE` (PR #438).
63	
64	## Decision Factors
65	
66	**Global default vs. per-stage knob.**
67	
68	- Global default: zero new code, but slow-failures on plan/review when
69	  raised, and doesn't match operator mental model. Rejected.
70	- Per-stage knob in template: ~150 LOC, matches ADR-015 v3 pattern,
71	  expresses the actual intent, ships sane defaults. Accepted.
72	
73	**Separate ADR vs. ADR-015 amendment.**
74	
75	- ADR-015 amendment: smaller. But ADR-015 is about *observability* (what
76	  the stage did, where to send the record). Router configuration is a
77	  different concern — it's about *how the stage's LLM call is shaped*.
78	  Folding them obscures both ADRs.
79	- Separate ADR (this one): makes the router-becomes-stage-aware contract
80	  change explicit. Accepted.
81	
82	**`router:` block vs. flat `router_timeout_s:` field.**
83	
84	- Flat field: simpler v1, but every future knob (tier, budget,
85	  model_override) needs another flat field at the stage level. Schema
86	  flattens, intent gets lost.
87	- Block (`router: { timeout_s: N, ... }`): mirrors the existing `io:`
88	  block. Future knobs slot in naturally without another ADR. Accepted.
89	
90	**Override precedence: who wins?**
91	
92	- Three layers: per-stage template, global env var, compile-time default.
93	- Per-stage MUST win the env var (otherwise operators can't pin a build
94	  stage's timeout regardless of what the env says).
95	- Env var MUST win the compile-time default (existing behavior; CLI
96	  invocations outside a pipeline still respect it).
97	- Decision: per-stage > env var > compile-time default.
98	
99	**Default value retention.**
100	
101	- Compile-time default stays at 300s. Single-shot CLI invocations and
102	  any stage that doesn't pin a template value still get the existing
103	  behavior. No silent behavior change for unmigrated templates.
104	
105	## Decision
106	
107	1. **Per-stage router configuration surface in the pipeline template.**
108	   New optional block under each stage:
109	
110	   ```yaml
111	   stages:
112	     - id: build
113	       gate: auto
114	       roles: [builder]
115	       io:
116	         destinations: [file, stdout]
117	         tail_lines: 200
118	       router:
119	         timeout_s: 900
120	   ```
121	
122	   First knob: `timeout_s`. Future knobs reserved (see §8). Absent
123	   `router:` block → no per-stage override (existing precedence kicks
124	   in).
125	
126	2. **Resolution precedence** (highest first):
127	   1. Per-stage template `router.<knob>`.
128	   2. Global env var `ZBUILD_ROUTER_TIMEOUT` (and analogous future env
129	      vars).
130	   3. Compile-time default in `core/router/route.sh` (300 for
131	      `timeout_s`, unchanged).
132	
133	3. **One chokepoint helper for resolution** — the router reads the
134	   resolved value via a small lookup that captures the precedence rule
135	   in one place. Pattern:
136	
137	   ```bash
138	   _route_resolve_timeout() {
139	       local v
140	       v="$(template_stage_router_timeout "${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}" 2>/dev/null || true)"
141	       [[ -n "$v" ]] && { printf '%s' "$v"; return 0; }
142	       printf '%s' "${ZBUILD_ROUTER_TIMEOUT:-300}"
143	   }
144	   ```
145	
146	   Centralising the precedence in `_route_resolve_*` helpers (rather
147	   than inlining at every consumer) means the rule is checkable by a
148	   future linter the same way ADR-004's redaction chokepoint is, and
149	   the same shape that ADR-015 used for `capture_stage_io`.

1	# ADR-054: Stage Contract
2	
3	**Status:** Accepted (2026-08-09)
4	**Date:** 2026-08-09
5	**Issue:** #1820
6	**Amended:** 2026-10-13 (#2366) — §6: result contract 3 carries ONE word, `outcome`, from one closed list the engine owns (Amendment at the end). Previously amended 2026-10-07 (#1798) — §4: a leaf stage whose verdict is fail-class ends the run unless its template marks it `blocking: false` (Amendment at the end).
7	**Amended:** 2026-09-16 (#2111) — §6: a rate limit observed by the router resolves to `unavailable`, not `throttled`. The engine now enforces `halt_unavailable` on the cycle dispatch path (it was announced only): the run ends `aborted` with `reason=llm_rate_limited` and the reset text under `.rate_limit.message`, state persisted for ADR-050 resume. `throttled` stays in the closed set with no rate-limit emitter. Waiting and retrying re-entered the same limit for five iterations on #1840/#1841, re-verifying an unchanged tree each time.
8	**Amended:** 2026-08-23 (#141) — §7: the three-actor table is run-keyed in every row; the **issue** is a second scope, and `release` gains the `always-run` attribute plus a `persist` sibling (ADR-059).
9	**Amended:** 2026-08-23 (#1920) — §7: the `release` "deletes nothing" promise scoped to the run's own lifecycle; operator-invoked reclamation (`zbuild cleanup --state-dirs`) named as a third actor with its own clock and guards.
10	**Amended:** 2026-08-12 (#1862) — §3.1 added: the engine exports dispatch identity (`ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE`, `ZBUILD_PLUGIN`, `ZBUILD_PLUGIN_KIND`, `ZBUILD_PLUGIN_DIR`) at `plugin_hook_call`, scoped to one dispatch. A plugin is self-defining about what it is and can never be self-defining about which stage it serves. `ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT` is explicitly excluded; identity is scrubbed by `env-scrub` per ADR-024, not exempted from it.
11	**Amends:**
12	- ADR-001 — the stage contract is two hooks (§1), rc ∈ {0,1} (§4), and one result file (§5). The rc=1→`kind: recovery` routing is deleted; it was never implemented and no recovery plugin was ever registered.
13	- ADR-021 — verdict and disposition are separated (§6); the informally-inherited `pass|warn|fail|unknown|error|corrupt_diff|block` set, which carried both axes in one string, is replaced.
14	- ADR-025 — the runner still owns the trap, but `cleanup` is no longer an abort-only notification: it is dispatched by a `teardown` stage with a `scope` (§7).
15	- ADR-045 — superseded by the same verdict/disposition split (§6).
16	**Related:** ADR-001 (plugin contract), ADR-013 (canonical stage list), ADR-017 (per-stage router config), ADR-047 (stage-agnostic mechanics — the parent principle this extends), ADR-055 (inter-stage data contract v2), ADR-056 (run+cleanup-only lifecycle)
17	
18	## Context
19	
20	**This ADR is a specification, not a description.** It states the contract Phase 0 (#1819) implements; each section names the issue that delivers it. Where the engine does not yet behave this way, that is recorded as the gap it is — the whole reason for writing it down.
21	
22	ADR-001 defined the general plugin contract for all plugin kinds. The stage-bound subset was never extracted, and the parts of ADR-001 that touched it were aspirational in a way nothing ever reconciled:
23	
24	| ADR-001 said | The engine did |
25	|---|---|
26	| Four hooks: `init`, `run`, `finalize`, `cleanup` | Five `plugin_hook_call` sites, **all `run`**. Three of the four were never called — including `cleanup`, which 20+ plugins nevertheless implement. |
27	| `rc=1` routes to `kind: recovery` plugins; `rc=2` is fatal | **No recovery plugin has ever been registered.** Stages return 5, 8, 9, 10, 11, 143. |
28	| `valid_verdicts` declares a plugin's vocabulary | ~~**No engine code reads it.** Adoption: 1 of 25.~~ **Closed by #1708**: adoption is 25 of 25, and `scripts/lib/lint-verdict-classify.sh` fails the build when a declared verdict is not classified. |
29	
30	The pattern is one defect, not three: **a declaration nothing enforces.** An unknown verdict draws a yellow glyph; an undeclared hook returns `0` silently; a zero-byte artifact passes the fail-closed scanner. Unrecognized is never a failure, so the document and the engine were free to drift apart for the life of the project.
31	
32	ADR-054 fixes the call and response surfaces — hooks, arguments, exit codes, the result file, and the verdict/disposition split. ADR-055 fixes the data and declaration surfaces. Together they are the interface Phase 0 enforces.
33	
34	### Why this precedes the rest of Initiative 1.3
35	
36	Initiative 1.3 (#1818) is one defect wearing different clothes across seven phases: the engine and its stages have no enforced interface. Phase 1 (#1794) makes a failing leaf stage stop the run — the single most valuable change in the milestone, and **unshippable without this contract**.
37	
38	Today a router timeout surfaces as `verdict=error`. Make a failing verdict terminal without first separating *what happened* from *what to do about it*, and a network hiccup on `intake` or `impact` becomes a dead run. `interrupted` and `throttled` exist so that the same event can stop a run that is genuinely broken and retry one that merely stalled. That is the whole reason the disposition vocabulary (§6) is a declared field rather than a string the engine re-interprets.
39	
40	The same dependency runs through the rest: Phase 3 cannot enforce declarations that were never load-bearing (ADR-055), Phase 4 cannot safely delete code whose reachability nothing can prove, and Phase 5's acceptance work measures assertions against a result file whose shape this ADR fixes. **Every phase either depends on this contract or is a consequence of not having had one.**
41	
42	## Decision
43	
44	### 1. The call surface: two hooks
45	
46	The contract has exactly **two** hooks:
47	
48	| Hook | Required | Invoked by |
49	|------|----------|------------|
50	| `run` | Yes | Every stage dispatch |
51	| `cleanup` | No | A `teardown` stage, with a `scope` (§7) |
52	
53	`init` and `finalize` are deleted from the contract. ADR-056 (#1828) carries out that deletion and owns the resulting lifecycle — including registration-time enforcement of `run` and the `rc=3` sentinel that distinguishes an absent optional hook from one that ran. This ADR does not restate those rules; it specifies the two surviving hooks' arguments (§2) and `cleanup`'s trigger and scope (§7).
54	
55	**What was true before this contract.** Three of the four hooks ADR-001 documented were never called: there are five `plugin_hook_call` sites in the engine and every one passes `run`. `init` and `finalize` were dead. `cleanup` was also dead — never dispatched by anything — yet **20+ plugins ship one**, written to a documented interface and drifting untested for the life of the project. That is the failure mode this ADR exists to end: a document describing a lifecycle the engine implemented one fifth of, with nothing reconciling the two.
56	
57	### 2. Hook signatures
58	
59	```
60	run(stage_id, state_file, resolved_inputs)
61	cleanup(stage_id, state_file, scope)
62	```
63	
64	- `stage_id` — the dispatching stage's id.
65	- `state_file` — absolute path to `pipeline-state.json`. Plugins derive `state_dir = dirname($2)` and `artifacts_dir = $state_dir/artifacts`.
66	- `resolved_inputs` — the engine resolves every input the manifest declares and hands them over. **A plugin never rebuilds a path.** Delivered by #1826; until then a plugin reads its declared inputs itself.
67	- `scope` — `release` or `purge` (§7).
68	
69	### 3. Runtime environment
70	
71	Run-time context is passed via env vars exported by the runner — never via positional args. The current set for stage-bound hooks:
72	
73	| Env var | Set by | Available to |
74	|---------|--------|--------------|
75	| `ZBUILD_GOAL` | runner | all hooks |
76	| `ZBUILD_ISSUE` | runner | all hooks (empty string when absent) |
77	| `ZBUILD_RUN_ID` | runner | all hooks |
78	| `ZBUILD_TARGET_PLATFORM` | runner (fanout strategy) | role-resolved hooks only |
79	| `ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE` | `plugin_hook_call` (§3.1) | all stage-bound hooks |
80	| `ZBUILD_PLUGIN` | `plugin_hook_call` (§3.1) | all stage-bound hooks |
81	| `ZBUILD_PLUGIN_KIND` | `plugin_hook_call` (§3.1) | all stage-bound hooks |
82	| `ZBUILD_PLUGIN_DIR` | `plugin_hook_call` (§3.1) | all stage-bound hooks |
83	
84	`ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE` (PR #438) is the key the per-stage router knob resolver uses to look up `router.timeout_s`, `router.max_turns`, `router.max_iterations`, `router.retries`, and `router.tier` (ADR-017).
85	
86	#### 3.1 Dispatch identity — amended 2026-08-12 (#1862)
87	
88	**The engine states, for exactly the span of one dispatch, which stage this is and which plugin serves it.** The single export point is `plugin_hook_call` (`core/plugin-registry/lifecycle.sh`).
89	
90	| Variable | Value | Source |
91	|---|---|---|
92	| `ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE` | the dispatching stage's name | `stage_id` — `$1` of the hook signature (§2) |
93	| `ZBUILD_PLUGIN` | the serving plugin's `id` | `$plugin_dir/manifest.yaml` |
94	| `ZBUILD_PLUGIN_KIND` | the serving plugin's `kind` | `$plugin_dir/manifest.yaml` |
95	| `ZBUILD_PLUGIN_DIR` | the serving plugin's directory | `$1` of `plugin_hook_call` |
96	| `ZBUILD_UNIT` | this unit's own name: the stage, or `<stage>.<element>` for a map member — `<stage>.<role>.<element>` when the map runs more than one role (amended 2026-10-03, #1706) | `stage_id` plus the element the map generator bakes into the work unit |
97	
98	**Why the engine and not the plugin.** A plugin is self-defining about *what it is* — `scripts/lib/plugin-bootstrap.sh` resolves `_ZBUILD_PLUGIN_DIR` from the plugin's own `BASH_SOURCE`, needing no engine. It can never be self-defining about *which stage it is currently serving*. Stage name, role and plugin id are three distinct namespaces and only the template holds the mapping: `review_lenses` (stage) is served by `review-lens` (plugin id) via role `review_lens`, and under `map:` all six lens members receive that one stage name. Everything keyed to the flow — the run timeline, `stage_statuses`, the per-stage router knobs — needs the stage name; introspection yields only the plugin id.
99	
100	The engine's answer cannot differ from the plugin's own: `plugin_hook_call` sources `plugin.sh` from the same directory it stamps, and reads `id`/`kind` from the same manifest the plugin would. It is the plugin's answer plus the axis the plugin cannot reach.
101	
102	**Why `plugin_hook_call`.** It is the only site reaching all four dispatch arms. The `map:` arm executes a generated standalone script (`core/pipeline/strategies/common.sh`) that the runner cannot export into — but `plugin_hook_call` is that script's last line.
103	
104	**Lifetime is one dispatch.** Declared `local -x`, not `export`. This reaches the lifecycle's own `plugin.*` emits (which fire outside the plugin subshell), reaches the subshell and anything it spawns, and unsets on return. Identity from stage *N* must not be visible during stage *N+1*; a plain `export` would trade a blank field for a stale one.
105	
106	**Each unit has its own name — amended 2026-10-03 (#1706).** Under `map:` every member receives the group's stage name, and that stays: the group is what template settings (router budgets, retries) are looked up by. But the members run at the same time, so anything a member writes or emits under the stage name alone collides. #2032 run 37066151065 lost red-team's diagnosis this way: the router named its error record `review_lenses-sync-error`, and the correctness lens's record overwrote it. So:
107	
108	- `ZBUILD_UNIT` is `<stage>.<element>` for a map member (the declared element, or the platform for a map over platforms) and the stage name otherwise. It lives for one dispatch, like the rest of this table. A stage dispatched from inside a member is named by its own stage. Enforced by `tests/unit/unit-name-test.sh` U1–U3.
109	- An engine event emitted inside a member carries `unit` in its envelope; an event outside a map carries no `unit` key, so every other envelope is unchanged. Enforced by U4.
110	- Per-member records are named by the unit; the router's error record is the first (`<unit>-sync-error`). Enforced by U5. The router's throttle and turn-budget markers stay keyed by stage, because the runner reads them at the group level, outside the members.
111	- A map that runs more than one role runs every role on every element, so the role is part of the name: `<stage>.<role>.<element>`. Enforced by U7.
112	- **Two units with one name never start together.** A map whose members would share a name is refused before any member starts (rc 1 — failed, per §4; the `strategy.unit_name_conflict` event names the duplicate). Enforced by U6.
113	
114	**Two owners, two questions, deliberately not merged.** `_ZBUILD_PLUGIN_DIR` (plugin-owned, set at source time) answers *where are my files on disk* and must keep working when a plugin is sourced with no engine present. `ZBUILD_PLUGIN_DIR` (engine-owned, set at dispatch) answers *who is this dispatch for*. In production they are always equal. Plugin code uses the former to locate its own assets; shared engine libraries use the latter to know whom they serve.
115	
116	**`ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT` is not identity and is not set here.** Every reader spells it `${ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT:-<repo default>}` — it is an operator override, and ADR-024 / `scripts/lib/persona-resolve.sh` forbid relying on it as a root. Engine-setting it would convert an override into a permanent pin. Derive from `ZBUILD_PLUGIN_DIR`.
117	
118	**Identity does not survive `env-scrub`.** Per ADR-024 the claude spawn is a fresh-user-shell subprocess that must not see `ZBUILD_*` pipeline state, and identity is pipeline state. Every consumer — the router's knob resolver, `stage_io_begin`, envelope stamping — runs in the parent scope before the spawn. `_zbuild_make_fresh_shell` scrubs identity along with everything else, and a regression guard asserts it.
119	
120	#### 3.2 Context is not data — added 2026-08-12 (#1768)
121	
122	The variables in §3 and §3.1 are **engine context**: they describe *the invocation*, not *the work*. Everything a stage consumes that describes the work is a **declared input**, resolved by the engine and handed to `run` (ADR-055 §1).
123	
124	| | Examples | How a stage gets it |
125	|---|---|---|
126	| **Context** — describes the invocation | run id, issue number, current stage, plugin identity (§3.1), cycle iteration, map element, target platform, state dir | ambient environment |
127	| **Data** — describes the work | a scope manifest, a plan, a diff, gate results, the issue body, the goal, the working tree | a declared input |
128	
129	The discriminator: **would a different template give this a different value for the same work?** Yes → context. No → data.
130	
131	This line matters because it was not drawn. Exactly one stage declares an external input today while ten plugins read `ZBUILD_ISSUE` straight from the environment — the issue body and the goal are *data*, arriving through the context channel, declared nowhere and checkable by nothing. ADR-055 §1.2 moves them; the variables above stay where they are.
132	
133	### 4. Exit codes (rc)
134	
135	Exit codes are **binary — everywhere, not only at the plugin boundary**:
136	
137	| rc | Meaning |
138	|----|---------|
139	| `0` | Success |
140	| `1` | Error |
141	
142	ADR-001 §"Error semantics" declared `rc=1` routes to `kind: recovery` plugins and `rc=2` is fatal. This routing was **never implemented** at the stage-dispatch layer. No recovery plugin has ever been registered. `rc=1` at the stage-dispatch layer has always been a terminal error. The rc table in ADR-001 is superseded.
143	
144	`rc=0` means "my result file is on disk, read it." `rc=1` means "I failed — read my result if present; if it is absent I died, and I am `broken`." **`rc=0` with a missing or unparseable result is a structural failure, not a warning.**
145	
146	Everything anything needs to say beyond those two facts belongs in the result file (§5), not in an exit code.
147	
148	**This binds engine-internal paths too.** The engine currently signals through a private rc vocabulary — `5` blocked, `6` cycle_abort, `8` blocking_member_failure, `9` llm_unavailable, `10` scope_too_large, `11` route_back, `130`/`143` signal. It is a vocabulary that grew one caller at a time, each reader mapping it differently, and it fails the same way the plugin-side table did: `cycle_orchestrator_run` special-cases only `8`, `11` and `130` and collapses every other abort rc to `4` (`config_invalid`), so a `cycle_abort` and a SIGTERM both surface as a configuration error. #1225 fixed that collapse for `11` alone.
149	
150	An integer channel with no declared vocabulary cannot be enforced, which is the defect this whole ADR exists to remove — exempting the engine from its own contract would reproduce it one layer down.
151	
152	So the control flow those codes carry moves onto declared channels: `disposition` (§6) for recoverability, and explicit routing state for the bounded backward edge (ADR-045) and blocking-member halt (ADR-013). Those mechanisms keep working; what changes is that a reader consults a declared field instead of re-interpreting a number. **#1823 owns the narrowing and the designs that re-home each signal**, and its acceptance is the enforcing check: no engine path returns or interprets an rc outside {0,1}, with a guard test enumerating the call sites.
153	
154	#### 4a. Where each signal goes (delivered by #1823)
155	
156	The destination is never new. Every one of these already had a declared channel the engine was setting alongside the number; the re-homing is to *read the word instead of the integer*, which is why `dispatch_rc_legacy_reason` names the vocabulary rather than inventing one.
157	
158	| rc | Re-homes onto | Owner |
159	|----|---------------|-------|
160	| `130`/`143` signal | `interrupted` (§6) — and the ADR-025 `.abort.signal` sentinel, which already carries abort across subshells | #1823 |
161	| `124` timeout | `interrupted` (§6). Never reaches the runner today: the router absorbs it and publishes `_ROUTE_LOOP_TERMINATED_REASON=router_timeout` | #1823 |
162	| rate limit | `unavailable` (§6) since #2111 (was `throttled`, #1823): the run ends, resumable when the limit resets | #1823 / #2111 |
163	| `9` llm_unavailable | `unavailable` (§6) — "halt; operator action required" is what rc=9 already meant | #1823 |
164	| `10` scope_too_large | `exhausted` (§6) — "more budget, or the work must shrink". The matching *verdict* string migrates in #1832. **(superseded 2026-09-25 by §6a / #2187 — now `out_of_turns`)** | #1823 / #1832 |
165	| `11` route_back | ADR-045 routing state (`_CYCLE_ROUTE_BACK_*`, `cycle.route_back`). The `route_target` vocabulary is #1767 | ADR-045 / #1767 |
166	| `8` blocking_member_failure | ADR-013's `blocking:true` halt and ADR-021's `disposition: terminal` member contract | ADR-013 / ADR-021 |
167	| `5` blocked | `_CYCLE_LAST_TERMINATED_REASON ∈ {blocked, no_committed_changes}` + `cycle.blocked` (ADR-021 #528/#1265) | ADR-021 |
168	| `6` cycle_abort | `_CYCLE_LAST_TERMINATED_REASON=cycle_abort` + `cycle.complete reason=` | ADR-021 |
169	| `4` config_invalid | `cycle.config.invalid` at load; the runtime collapse-to-4 catch-all has no channel and is a known gap | ADR-021 |
170	
171	**`5`, `6`, `8`, `11` and `4` deliberately map to NO disposition.** They are control-flow decisions the cycle made, not statements about whether a stage got far enough to produce a verdict worth reading. Forcing them into §6's set would be exactly the invented default this ADR forbids.
172	
173	**Two recorded discrepancies, both resolved by #1860 (2026-08-20).** ADR-026 said `cycle_abort` is rc=5 in four places, while ADR-045, this ADR and the code all say 6 — #1860 annotated the four stale sites as historical. And `_cycle_handle_terminal_rc` had a `130)` arm but no `143)` arm; #1860 merged them into `130|143) reason="aborted"` so SIGTERM and SIGINT agree at the orchestrator fan-in as well as at the dispatch boundary.
174	
175	#### 4b. Coexistence: v1 keeps its rc, v2 is narrowed
176	
177	**(superseded 2026-10-08 by the #1850 amendment below — v1 is refused at load; every stage is narrowed; the inventory is zero)**
178	
179	**The narrowing is gated on `result_contract`, not applied to every plugin at once.**
180	
181	A v1 plugin's exit code is still its *only* channel. `plan` reports `scope_too_large` as rc=10 and has no result field in which to say it; `design`, `validate` and `monitor` all `return 2` for a missing `state_file` per ADR-001 §Runtime. Narrowing every plugin today would delete the meaning of all 25 in a single step, and the engine would keep running past conditions that currently stop it — an oversized scope would no longer abort.
182	
183	So:
184	
185	| Stage speaks | rc | Held to the `disposition` dictionary? |
186	|---|---|---|
187	| `result_contract: 1` (today's 25 plugins) | passes through **unchanged** | No — it declares no disposition, and absence is not an off-set word |
188	| `result_contract: 2` | narrowed to **{0,1}** | Yes — an off-set word is a structural failure carrying `contract_violation:unknown_disposition:<word>` |
189	
190	A v2 stage has somewhere else to say everything its rc was carrying, which is precisely what makes narrowing safe for it and unsafe for the others. This is the same versioned coexistence §6 already uses for the vocabulary — consulted at `result_contract >= 2` and nowhere else — and the same one §5 uses for strictness.
191	
192	The classification of an `rc=1` that left no result (§4a) is **additive and applies to both versions**: an unmigrated stage gets an honest `interrupted`/`throttled`/`broken` on the disposition channel today, with no change to the rc it reports.
193	
194	**End state.** #1850 drops the v1 reader, the version gate and the legacy mapping together. At that point narrowing is unconditional, every stage is held to the dictionary, and the guard's enumerated inventory goes to zero — becoming the plain rule stated in §4. Until then `tests/unit/dispatch-rc-guard-test.sh` ratchets it: a count may fall, never rise, so the vocabulary cannot grow while it is being retired.
195	
196	### 5. The result file
197	
198	One file. The primary artifact declared in the stage's manifest (`outputs[primary: true]`), read after `run` returns. Mandatory keys:

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# [#1801/SPEC-1] A run hook that hangs is killed at the per-stage timeout on
3	# every dispatch route — map, fanout, sequential strategy, roleless leaf, cycle
4	# member, parallel-group member, and always_run — and the stage ends with
5	# disposition timed_out naming the stage and the limit.
6	#
7	# [#1801/SPEC-10] _runner_dispatch_always_run and _orch_local_collect_results
8	# kill through zbuild_pg_kill; no hand-rolled TERM/KILL sequence remains for
9	# stage dispatch.
10	#
11	# All dispatch routes reach plugin_hook_call in lifecycle.sh; the single
12	# watchdog there covers every route. These tests FAIL on pre-change code
13	# (where lifecycle.sh has no watchdog) and PASS after the change.
14	set -euo pipefail
15	
16	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
17	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
18	
19	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
20	source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
21	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
22	source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"
23	
24	print_test_header "[#1801/SPEC-1/SPEC-10] per-dispatch stage timeout watchdog"
25	setup_test_env "stage-timeout-dispatch"
26	
27	_lc="$REPO_ROOT/core/plugin-registry/lifecycle.sh"
28	
29	# ─── Extract plugin_hook_call body for inspection ────────────────────────────
30	_phc_body=""
31	if [[ -f "$_lc" ]]; then
32	    _phc_body="$(awk '/^plugin_hook_call\(\) \{/{p=1} p{print} p && /^\}$/{exit}' "$_lc" 2>/dev/null || true)"
33	fi
34	
35	# ─── [#1801/SPEC-1] lifecycle.sh has a per-dispatch timeout watchdog ──────────
36	print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-1] plugin_hook_call has a timeout watchdog for the run hook"
37	
38	if [[ -z "$_phc_body" ]]; then
39	    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] plugin_hook_call is defined in lifecycle.sh" "not found"
40	else
41	    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] plugin_hook_call is defined in lifecycle.sh"
42	
43	    # The watchdog must be armed only for the `run` hook (not cleanup/other hooks).
44	    # Check for a guard like `[[ "$hook_name" == "run" ]]` near the timeout code.
45	    if grep -qE '"run"' <<< "$_phc_body" && grep -q 'zbuild_pg_kill\|zbuild_pid_kill' <<< "$_phc_body"; then
46	        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] watchdog in plugin_hook_call is guarded to run hook only"
47	    else
48	        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] watchdog in plugin_hook_call is guarded to run hook only" \
49	            "zbuild_pg_kill/zbuild_pid_kill not found inside plugin_hook_call — no per-dispatch watchdog"
50	    fi
51	fi
52	
53	# ─── [#1801/SPEC-1] the watchdog writes timed_out disposition ─────────────────
54	print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-1] watchdog writes disposition timed_out"
55	
56	# The watchdog must call the disposition layer with 'timed_out' when it fires.
57	# Check lifecycle.sh and disposition-writing helpers used from within lifecycle.sh.
58	_timed_out_found=0
59	if grep -q 'timed_out' "$_lc" 2>/dev/null; then
60	    _timed_out_found=1
61	fi
62	# Also check that the runner or a helper wires the watchdog result to timed_out
63	_runner="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"
64	if grep -q 'timed_out' "$_runner" 2>/dev/null; then
65	    _timed_out_found=1
66	fi
67	
68	if [[ "$_timed_out_found" -eq 1 ]]; then
69	    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] timed_out disposition is used in the dispatch path"
70	else
71	    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] timed_out disposition is used in the dispatch path" \
72	        "'timed_out' not found in lifecycle.sh or runner.sh — timeout result cannot produce the required disposition"
73	fi
74	
75	# After the change: the timed_out event must name the stage and the limit.
76	# The requirement says "ends with disposition timed_out naming the stage and the limit".
77	# Check that the emit_event call for plugin.run.timed_out in lifecycle.sh carries
78	# both stage= and timeout_s= fields.
79	_timed_out_event_ctx=""
80	if [[ -f "$_lc" ]]; then
81	    _timed_out_event_ctx="$(grep -A4 'plugin\.run\.timed_out' "$_lc" 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' ' || true)"
82	fi
83	if grep -q 'stage=' <<< "$_timed_out_event_ctx" && grep -q 'timeout_s=' <<< "$_timed_out_event_ctx"; then
84	    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] timed_out event names the stage (stage=) and the limit (timeout_s=)"
85	else
86	    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] timed_out event names the stage (stage=) and the limit (timeout_s=)" \
87	        "plugin.run.timed_out event in lifecycle.sh is missing stage= or timeout_s= field"
88	fi
89	
90	# ─── [#1801/SPEC-1] every dispatch route reaches plugin_hook_call ─────────────
91	print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-1] all dispatch routes lead through plugin_hook_call"
92	
93	# The design states: all dispatch routes — map, fanout, sequential strategy,
94	# roleless leaf, cycle member, parallel-group member, always_run — reach
95	# plugin_hook_call. Verify that each strategy file and the runner itself calls
96	# plugin_hook_call (not a private bypass).
97	for _sf in \
98	    core/pipeline/strategies/fanout.sh \
99	    core/pipeline/strategies/sequential.sh \
100	    core/pipeline/strategies/map.sh \
101	    core/pipeline/runner.sh; do
102	    _file="$REPO_ROOT/$_sf"
103	    [[ -f "$_file" ]] || continue
104	    if grep -q 'plugin_hook_call' "$_file"; then
105	        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] $_sf reaches plugin_hook_call (route covered by watchdog)"
106	    else
107	        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] $_sf reaches plugin_hook_call (route covered by watchdog)" \
108	            "plugin_hook_call not found — this dispatch route would bypass the watchdog"
109	    fi
110	done
111	
112	# ─── [#1801/SPEC-10] no hand-rolled TERM/KILL in lifecycle.sh for dispatch ────
113	print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-10] lifecycle.sh has no hand-rolled TERM/KILL for stage dispatch"
114	
115	if [[ -n "$_phc_body" ]]; then
116	    # After the change: no `kill -TERM` or `kill -KILL` hand-rolled in
117	    # plugin_hook_call itself — these are replaced by zbuild_pg_kill.
118	    # Allow lines that are purely comments.
119	    _hand_rolled=""
120	    _hand_rolled="$(grep -E 'kill -TERM|kill -KILL' <<< "$_phc_body" | grep -v '^\s*#' || true)"
121	    if [[ -n "$_hand_rolled" ]]; then
122	        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-10] plugin_hook_call has no hand-rolled TERM/KILL for stage dispatch" \
123	            "found: $(printf '%s' "$_hand_rolled" | head -3 | tr '\n' '|') — replace with zbuild_pg_kill"
124	    else
125	        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-10] plugin_hook_call has no hand-rolled TERM/KILL for stage dispatch"
126	    fi
127	fi
128	
129	# ─── [#1801/SPEC-10] _orch_local_collect_results uses zbuild_pg_kill ──────────
130	print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-10] _orch_local_collect_results uses zbuild_pg_kill"
131	
132	_le="$REPO_ROOT/core/orch/local_engine.sh"
133	if [[ ! -f "$_le" ]]; then
134	    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-10] core/orch/local_engine.sh exists" "not found"
135	else
136	    if grep -q 'zbuild_pg_kill\|zbuild_pid_kill' "$_le"; then
137	        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-10] local_engine.sh uses zbuild_pg_kill/zbuild_pid_kill"
138	    else
139	        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-10] local_engine.sh uses zbuild_pg_kill/zbuild_pid_kill" \
140	            "not found — _orch_local_collect_results still has a hand-rolled kill sequence"
141	    fi
142	
143	    # The old _orch_local_kill_slot is replaced; if it still exists, that is a bug.
144	    if grep -q '_orch_local_kill_slot' "$_le"; then
145	        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-10] _orch_local_kill_slot is removed from local_engine.sh" \
146	            "still present — the hand-rolled kill helper was not replaced by zbuild_pg_kill"
147	    else
148	        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-10] _orch_local_kill_slot is removed from local_engine.sh"
149	    fi
150	fi
151	
152	# ─── watchdog is backend-agnostic: lifecycle is above backends ────────────────
153	print_test_section "watchdog in lifecycle.sh is backend-agnostic (above the backend layer)"
154	
155	# The watchdog's position in lifecycle.sh (plugin_hook_call) means it fires
156	# regardless of which orch backend is active — the backends dispatch work units
157	# that ultimately call plugin_hook_call. Verify orch-mock still routes through it.
158	_mock_plugin="$REPO_ROOT/plugins/tool/orch-mock/plugin.sh"
159	if [[ ! -f "$_mock_plugin" ]]; then
160	    assert_fail "plugins/tool/orch-mock/plugin.sh exists" "not found"
161	else
162	    # orch-mock dispatches work units that call plugin_hook_call;
163	    # the backend itself does not arm or disarm the watchdog.
164	    assert_pass "orch-mock plugin exists (backend-agnostic watchdog can be tested with it)"
165	fi
166	
167	# ─── ruflo-hive carries no suppressing TERM/KILL sequence ─────────────────────
168	print_test_section "orch-ruflo-hive/plugin.sh has no TERM/KILL for stage dispatch"
169	
170	_hive="$REPO_ROOT/plugins/tool/orch-ruflo-hive/plugin.sh"
171	if [[ ! -f "$_hive" ]]; then
172	    assert_fail "plugins/tool/orch-ruflo-hive/plugin.sh exists" "not found"
173	else
174	    # The hive plugin must not have a kill -TERM / kill -KILL that would intercept
175	    # the lifecycle-level watchdog's signal before it reaches the hook subshell.
176	    # (Pool-management kills in the backend's own shutdown are acceptable.)
177	    _hive_kills=""
178	    _hive_kills="$(grep -n 'kill -TERM\|kill -KILL' "$_hive" | grep -v '^\s*#' || true)"
179	    if [[ -n "$_hive_kills" ]]; then
180	        assert_fail "orch-ruflo-hive/plugin.sh carries no TERM/KILL for stage dispatch" \
181	            "found kill -TERM/-KILL in ruflo-hive — may suppress lifecycle-level watchdog signal:" \
182	            "$(printf '%s' "$_hive_kills" | head -5 | tr '\n' '|')"
183	    else
184	        assert_pass "orch-ruflo-hive/plugin.sh carries no TERM/KILL for stage dispatch"
185	    fi
186	fi
187	
188	cleanup_test_env
189	print_test_results
190	exit $((FAIL > 0))

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# [#1801/SPEC-7] Guard: removing ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT from the three strategy files
3	# means the per-dispatch watchdog is the only stage time limit.
4	#
5	# Before this change the strategy files had `orch_collect … --timeout
6	# "${ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT:-300}"` as a flat ceiling; a plan dispatch running
7	# longer than 300 s would have been killed even when its `stage_timeout_s`
8	# allowed more. After the change, orch_collect is called without --timeout (or
9	# with no ceiling), leaving the per-dispatch watchdog in lifecycle.sh as the
10	# only limit.
11	#
12	# The assertions are source-level: they verify that each strategy file no
13	# longer carries the flat ceiling. This test FAILS on pre-change code
14	# (where ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT still appears) and PASSES after the change.
15	set -euo pipefail
16	
17	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
18	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
19	
20	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
21	source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
22	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
23	source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"
24	
25	print_test_header "[#1801/SPEC-7] ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT absent from strategy files"
26	
27	# ─── Each strategy file must not reference ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT ───────────────
28	# These are the three files the design names: fanout.sh, sequential.sh, map.sh.
29	# Every occurrence of ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT pins a flat ceiling that the per-dispatch
30	# watchdog is meant to replace.
31	
32	for _sf in \
33	    core/pipeline/strategies/fanout.sh \
34	    core/pipeline/strategies/sequential.sh \
35	    core/pipeline/strategies/map.sh; do
36	
37	    _file="$REPO_ROOT/$_sf"
38	    if [[ ! -f "$_file" ]]; then
39	        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-7] $_sf exists" "file not found: $_file"
40	        continue
41	    fi
42	
43	    if grep -q 'ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT' "$_file"; then
44	        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-7] $_sf carries no ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT flat ceiling" \
45	            "ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT still present — a plan dispatch longer than the default 300 s" \
46	            "would be killed before its stage_timeout_s expires"
47	    else
48	        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-7] $_sf carries no ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT flat ceiling"
49	    fi
50	
51	    # Also verify orch_collect/orch_wait calls carry no --timeout flag.
52	    # A hard-coded --timeout N in the orch call would impose a flat ceiling
53	    # independent of ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT and would kill long-but-valid dispatches.
54	    if grep -qE 'orch_collect.*--timeout|orch_wait.*--timeout' "$_file"; then
55	        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-7] $_sf orch_collect/orch_wait carry no --timeout flag" \
56	            "--timeout found in orch call — imposes a flat ceiling that overrides stage_timeout_s"
57	    else
58	        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-7] $_sf orch_collect/orch_wait carry no --timeout flag"
59	    fi
60	done
61	
62	print_test_results
63	exit $((FAIL > 0))

5	#

7	# recognized template field and _TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_* is never exported)
8	# and PASS after the change.
9	set -euo pipefail
10	
11	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

23	
24	_MINIMAL_HEAD='id: t
25	name: T
26	extends: null
27	defaults:
28	  strategy: fanout
29	'

35	# ─── Tier 1: template value beats ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S ─────────────────────
36	print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-3] template stage_timeout_s beats ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S"
37

40	  - alpha

45	  stage_timeout_s: 7200
46	  io:
47	    destinations: [file]

55	# ─── Tier 2: ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S beats the 5400 s default ─────────────────

64	  roles: [intake]
65	  io:
66	    destinations: [file]

2	# Integration test (#1829, ADR-054 §7): the runner dispatches cleanup(release)
3	# on EVERY exit path from a run — success, non-zero rc, the SIGINT propagation
4	# chain, an external SIGTERM, and an external timeout.
5	#
6	# This is the acceptance criterion the mechanism exists for: a stage's live
7	# resources must be freed however the run ends. A single missed exit path leaks
8	# whatever that stage spawned (#1748: suites observed alive 15+ min after exit).
9	#
10	# Why SIGINT is driven by the stage rather than `kill -INT`: this harness starts
11	# non-interactively with SIGINT inherited as SIG_IGN, and POSIX forbids a child
12	# from un-ignoring it — so `kill -INT` is silently dropped and the assertion
13	# would pass standalone while proving nothing. The repo's existing
14	# sigint-aborts-pipeline-test.sh drives the same chain the same way: the child
15	# returns 130, which is exactly what the kernel produces on Ctrl-C. Since #1850
16	# (ADR-054 §4, ADR-025) a signal is a recorded WORD, not an rc, so the stage
17	# also arms the abort sentinel (empty = sigint), as the runner's INT trap in
18	# the process group would.
19	#
20	# Assertion in every case: the stub stages' cleanup hooks recorded `release`
21	# (and never `purge`) in the marker file.
22	set -euo pipefail

68	export ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=0

70	# #978: job-control PG forwarding is roster-agnostic — T1 probes the runner
71	# shell's monitor-mode via intake, and T2 signals mid-build and asserts test
72	# never runs. Drive a MINIMAL 3-leaf fixture (intake → build → test) instead of
73	# pinning to the standard roster (retired in #979). #1270: install the fixture as
74	# a per-repo `.zbuild/templates/` overlay in a temp repo and run with CWD = that
75	# repo (the resolver reads the overlay from $PWD). intake/build/test get custom
76	# bodies below.

78	install_template_overlay "$OVERLAY_REPO" resume-minimal
79	mock_plugin_factory "intake" "agent" 0 >/dev/null
80	mock_plugin_factory "build"  "agent" 0 >/dev/null
81	mock_plugin_factory "test"   "tool"  0 >/dev/null
82	
83	# Probe intake records $- (set of shell option flags) to a marker so we
84	# can introspect whether the runner shell has 'm' (monitor mode) set.
85	cat > "$PROBE_PLUGINS/agent/intake/plugin.sh" <<PROBE
86	intake_run() {
87	    echo "dash=\$-" > "${PROBE_OPTS_FILE}"
88	    set -o | grep -E '^monitor' >> "${PROBE_OPTS_FILE}" 2>/dev/null || true
89	    $(mock_result_line intake)
90	    return 0
91	}
92	PROBE
93	
94	# Run with flag OFF.
95	: > "$PROBE_OPTS_FILE"
96	unset ZBUILD_RUNNER_JOB_CONTROL
97	rm -f "$PROBE_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json"
98	set +e
99	# #1270: CWD = overlay repo so the resolver finds the resume-minimal fixture.
100	( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template resume-minimal --goal "w15h probe flag-off" ) \
101	    >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/runner-off.stdout" 2>"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/runner-off.stderr"
102	rc_off=$?
103	set -e
104	opts_off="$(cat "$PROBE_OPTS_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo "")"
105	
106	# Run with flag ON.
107	: > "$PROBE_OPTS_FILE"
108	export ZBUILD_RUNNER_JOB_CONTROL=1
109	rm -f "$PROBE_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json"
110	set +e
111	( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template resume-minimal --goal "w15h probe flag-on" ) \
112	    >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/runner-on.stdout" 2>"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/runner-on.stderr"
113	rc_on=$?
114	set -e
115	opts_on="$(cat "$PROBE_OPTS_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo "")"
116	
117	# Both runs must exit 0.
118	assert_eq "flag-off probe run rc=0" "0" "$rc_off"
119	assert_eq "flag-on  probe run rc=0" "0" "$rc_on"
120	# #2193: a probe that exits non-zero must say why — CI showed only "got: 1".
121	for _pr in off on; do
122	    _rcv="rc_$_pr"
123	    if [[ "${!_rcv}" != "0" ]]; then
124	        echo "--- runner-$_pr.stderr (tail) ---" >&2
125	        tail -30 "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/runner-$_pr.stderr" >&2 2>/dev/null || true
126	    fi
127	done
128	
129	# Flag-off: $- must NOT contain 'm'; set -o monitor must be off.
130	if grep -qE 'dash=[^m]*$|dash=[^m]*[^m]*$' <<< "$opts_off" && \
131	   grep -qE '^monitor[[:space:]]+off$' <<< "$opts_off"; then
132	    assert_pass "flag-off: monitor mode OFF in runner shell"
133	else
134	    # Looser check: dash line should not have 'm'.
135	    _opts_off_1="$(head -1 <<< "$opts_off")"
136	    if grep -qv 'm' <<< "$_opts_off_1"; then
137	        assert_pass "flag-off: monitor mode OFF in runner shell (dash check)"
138	    else
139	        assert_fail "flag-off: monitor mode OFF in runner shell" \
140	            "got: $opts_off"
141	    fi
142	fi
143	
144	# Flag-on: $- must contain 'm' OR set -o monitor must be on.
145	_opts_on_1="$(head -1 <<< "$opts_on")"
146	if grep -q 'm' <<< "$_opts_on_1" || \
147	   grep -qE '^monitor[[:space:]]+on$' <<< "$opts_on"; then
148	    assert_pass "flag-on: monitor mode ON in runner shell"
149	else
150	    assert_fail "flag-on: monitor mode ON in runner shell" \
151	        "got: $opts_on"
152	fi
153	
154	# ─── T2: SIGTERM with flag-on still produces exit 1 + Wave 15-B chain ────────
155	print_test_section "T2: end-to-end SIGTERM with flag-on (regression of trap chain)"
156	
157	# Reuse $PROBE_PLUGINS (= TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins). Override build/test/intake.
158	E2E_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state-e2e"
159	E2E_EVENTS_JSONL="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events-e2e/events.jsonl"
160	export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$E2E_STATE_DIR"
161	export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events-e2e"
162	export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$E2E_EVENTS_JSONL"
163	mkdir -p "$E2E_STATE_DIR" "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events-e2e"
164	export ZBUILD_RUNNER_JOB_CONTROL=1
165	
166	E2E_BUILD_STARTED="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/e2e-build-started"
167	E2E_TEST_RAN="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/e2e-test-ran"
168	export E2E_BUILD_STARTED E2E_TEST_RAN
169	
170	# Restore intake to a no-op (was overridden by probe).
171	cat > "$PROBE_PLUGINS/agent/intake/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
172	intake_run() { $(mock_result_line intake); return 0; }
173	PLUG
174	
175	# Build plugin: short polling loop so the trap can fire within budget.
176	# Note: under flag-on, `set -m` puts the plugin subshell in its own PGID
177	# so a kernel-pgrp TERM to the runner does NOT reach the subshell directly.
178	# The runner's trap therefore fires only after the foreground subshell
179	# returns naturally — bounded by the loop length here.
180	cat > "$PROBE_PLUGINS/agent/build/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
181	build_run() {
182	    : > "${E2E_BUILD_STARTED}"
183	    local _i
184	    for _i in \$(seq 1 30); do
185	        sleep 0.1
186	    done
187	    $(mock_result_line build)
188	    return 0
189	}
190	PLUG
191	cat > "$PROBE_PLUGINS/tool/test/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
192	test_run() { : > "${E2E_TEST_RAN}"; $(mock_result_line test); return 0; }
193	PLUG
194	
195	# #1270: the runner resolves the fixture from $PWD, so cd into the overlay repo
196	# before exec-ing it. `exec` replaces the wrapper shell so $! is the runner PID.
197	if command -v setsid >/dev/null 2>&1; then
198	    setsid bash -c 'cd "$1" && exec bash "$2" --template resume-minimal --goal "$3"' \
199	        _ "$OVERLAY_REPO" "$RUNNER" "w15h e2e" \
200	        >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/runner-e2e.stdout" 2>"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/runner-e2e.stderr" &

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# core/pipeline/strategies/sequential.sh — serialized per-platform dispatch (issue #200/#222)
3	# ADR-009: platforms run one at a time; always halts on the first collect failure.
4	# Depends on core/orch/contract.sh being sourced first by the caller (runner.sh).
5	# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail; do not add set -euo pipefail here.
6	
7	[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_STRATEGY_SEQUENTIAL_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
8	_ZBUILD_STRATEGY_SEQUENTIAL_LOADED=1
9	
10	_ZBUILD_STRATEGIES_DIR_SEQ="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
11	source "${_ZBUILD_STRATEGIES_DIR_SEQ}/common.sh"
12	
13	# ─── _strategy_run_sequential ────────────────────────────────────────────────
14	# Usage: _strategy_run_sequential <pool_id> <stage> <roles_out> <state_file> <plugins_root>
15	#   pool_id    — caller-supplied, already validated
16	#   stage      — stage name
17	#   roles_out  — newline-delimited list of role names
18	#   state_file — path to pipeline state file
19	#   plugins_root — path to plugins directory
20	#
21	# Dispatches one work unit at a time via orch_dispatch + orch_collect.
22	# Halts on first failure (does not continue to next platform/role).
23	# Always calls orch_shutdown on exit (success or failure).
24	# Artifact enforcement happens per work unit inside plugin_hook_call (#1906).
25	#
26	# Returns:
27	#   0 — all succeeded
28	#   1 — any collect/dispatch failure
29	#   4 — no plugin found for any role (caller may fall back to stage-id lookup)
30	_strategy_run_sequential() {
31	    # #1850 (ADR-054 §4): rc is 0 or 1; WHY rides this word, which the caller
32	    # reads in the same shell — ok | partial | empty | no_plugin | bad_dimension
33	    # | infra_failed | failed.
34	    _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="failed"
35	    local pool_id="$1" stage="$2" roles_out="$3" state_file="$4" plugins_root="$5"
36	    local any_plugin_found=false
37	
38	    local role platform plugin_dir wu prc
39	    while IFS= read -r role; do
40	        [[ -z "$role" ]] && continue
41	        for platform in "${_DETECTED_PLATFORMS[@]}"; do
42	            plugin_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$role" "$platform" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
43	            [[ -z "$plugin_dir" ]] && \
44	                plugin_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$role" "" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
45	            [[ -z "$plugin_dir" ]] && continue
46	            any_plugin_found=true
47	
48	            wu="$(_strategy_make_work_unit "$plugin_dir" "$stage" "$state_file" "$platform")" || {
49	                warn "sequential: failed to create work unit for role=$role platform=$platform" || true
50	                orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
51	                return 1
52	            }
53	
54	            orch_dispatch "$pool_id" "$wu" >/dev/null || {
55	                warn "sequential: orch_dispatch failed for role=$role platform=$platform" || true
56	                rm -f "$wu" 2>/dev/null || true
57	                orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
58	                return 1
59	            }
60	
61	            prc=0
62	            orch_collect "$pool_id" || prc=$?
63	            rm -f "$wu" 2>/dev/null || true
64	
65	            if [[ $prc -ne 0 ]]; then
66	                warn "sequential: stage=$stage role=$role platform=$platform failed (rc=$prc)" || true
67	                orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
68	                return 1
69	            fi
70	
71	        done
72	    done <<< "$roles_out"
73	
74	    orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
75	    $any_plugin_found || { _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="no_plugin"; return 1; }
76	    _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="ok"
77	    return 0
78	}
